purpose: Lorlatinib is used to treat a type of lung cancer called non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has a specific gene change called ALK-positive. It is often used when other similar medicines have stopped working or as an initial treatment for this type of cancer.
how_it_works: Your cancer has a specific genetic mutation that acts like a faulty switch, telling cancer cells to grow out of control. Lorlatinib works by blocking that faulty switch, called ALK, so cancer cells can no longer grow and spread as easily. Think of it like putting a lock on the switch so cancer cannot turn itself on.
common_side_effects: Swelling in your legs or arms, high cholesterol or triglycerides (fats in your blood), feeling mentally foggy or having memory problems, mood changes, tingling or numbness in hands and feet, weight gain, tiredness, and joint or muscle pain.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious effects on your thinking, mood, and behavior — including depression, hallucinations, or personality changes. Tell your doctor right away if you or your family notice any unusual mood or mental changes. It can also raise cholesterol levels significantly, so regular blood tests are needed. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine. Do not take it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm your baby. Always tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, as many drugs can interact with lorlatinib.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 100 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or split it. If you miss a dose and it has been less than 4 hours, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 4 hours, skip that dose and take the next one on schedule.
